heading: Liji 2 · Tan Gong 檀弓 · Than Kung · Tan Gong I.i.13 … Tan Gong I.i.25

items.text: Obey your father even to death; do not wound his heart or flee his sentence.
items.quote: Is there any state where the (sacredness) of a father is not recognised? Where should I go to obviate this charge?
items.conflict: Suicide violates the sixth commandment; obedience to parents is in the Lord, not to unlawful death (Exodus 20:13; Ephesians 6:1).

items.text: Mourn a parent with weeping and wailing, sackcloth, and mourning food, as is required from the Son of Heaven down.
items.quote: the sorrow declared in the weeping and wailing, the feelings expressed in the robe of sackcloth... extend from the son of Heaven to all.

items.text: Obey a father's dying wish for correct rites; do not put fond indulgence above virtue.
items.quote: Your love of me is not equal to his. A superior man loves another on grounds of virtue; a little man's love of another is seen in his indulgence.

items.text: At a father's death appear overcome; after burial look sorrowful; at the first and second years' end show the appointed grief.
items.quote: When (a father) has just died, (the son) should appear quite overcome... at the end of the second year's, he should have a vague and unreliant look.

items.text: Mourn your mother-in-law with sackcloth and bound hair; keep it neither very high nor broad.
items.quote: Do not make it very high, nor very broad. Have the hair-pin of hazel-wood, and the hair-knots (hanging down) eight inches.

heading: Liji 2 · Tan Gong 檀弓 · Than Kung · Tan Gong I.ii.16 … Tan Gong I.ii.27

items.text: Follow your father's coffin with eager affection and return as if in doubt.
items.quote: He went as if he were full of eager affection. He came back looking as if he were in doubt.

items.text: Avenge your father or mother: sleep on straw, take no office, refuse to live under the same heaven with the slayer, and fight him at once.
items.quote: He should sleep on straw, with his shield for a pillow; he should not take office; he must be determined not to live with the slayer under the same heaven.
items.conflict: Vengeance belongs to God (Rom 12:19); do not return evil for evil.

items.text: Avenge your brother: you may take office, but not in the same state as the slayer; if sent on a ruler's mission, do not fight him then.
items.quote: He may take office, but not in the same state with the slayer.
items.conflict: Vengeance belongs to God (Rom 12:19); do not return evil for evil.

items.text: Do not take the lead in avenging a slain cousin; support the chief avenger from behind with your weapon in hand.
items.quote: He should not take the lead in avenging. If he whom it chiefly concerns is able, he should support him from behind with his weapon.
items.conflict: Vengeance belongs to God (Rom 12:19); do not return evil for evil.

items.text: When mourning an elder sister, stand with the right hand uppermost.
items.quote: I place my hands so, because I am mourning for an elder sister.

items.text: In mourning the dead, let exceeding grief with deficient rites be better than little grief with superabounding rites; and in sacrifice, let exceeding reverence with deficient rites be better than excess of rites with little reverence.
items.quote: exceeding grief with deficient rites is better than little grief with superabounding rites; and in sacrifice, exceeding reverence with deficient rites is better than excess of rites with little reverence.

heading: Liji 2 · Tan Gong 檀弓 · Than Kung · Tan Gong I.ii.39 … Tan Gong I.iii.6

items.text: Wear full mourning for a brother's son as for your own son, drawing him near.
items.citation: Liji, Tan Gong I.ii.39 … Tan Gong I.iii.6
items.quote: The mourning worn for the son of a brother should be the same as for one's own son.

items.text: Do not wear mourning for an elder brother's wife or for a younger brother; keep the distance between them.
items.citation: Liji, Tan Gong I.ii.39 … Tan Gong I.iii.6
items.quote: An elder brother's wife and his younger brother do not wear mourning for each other.
items.needs_role: elder brother's wife and younger brother

items.text: Wear only slight mourning for a married aunt who has died, because her own household will give her full mourning.
items.citation: Liji, Tan Gong I.ii.39 … Tan Gong I.iii.6
items.quote: Slight mourning is worn for an aunt ... when they have been married.

items.text: Wear only slight mourning for a married sister who has died, because her husband's household will give her full mourning.
items.citation: Liji, Tan Gong I.ii.39 … Tan Gong I.iii.6
items.quote: Slight mourning is worn for ... an elder or younger sister, (when they have been married).

items.text: When your father dies, wail for him in your apartment, not in the lane.
items.citation: Liji, Tan Gong I.ii.39 … Tan Gong I.iii.6
items.quote: Return to your apartment, and wail for him there.

items.text: When furnishing the dead, use vessels of the eye of fancy, not fully useful vessels, treating them as spiritual intelligences.
items.citation: Liji, Tan Gong I.ii.39 … Tan Gong I.iii.6
items.quote: They are called vessels to the eye of fancy; that is, (the dead) are thus treated as if they were spiritual intelligences.

items.text: Do not prepare mourning goods beforehand; make only what can be finished in a day or two.
items.citation: Liji, Tan Gong I.ii.39 … Tan Gong I.iii.6
items.quote: A superior man is ashamed to prepare (beforehand) all that he may require in discharging his mourning rites.

items.text: If you have shared a fireplace with the husband of a maternal cousin or the wife of a maternal uncle, wear three months' mourning for them.
items.citation: Liji, Tan Gong I.ii.39 … Tan Gong I.iii.6
items.quote: If they have eaten together from the same fireplace, the three months' mourning should be worn.
items.needs_role: husband of a maternal cousin and wife of a maternal uncle

heading: Liji 2 · Tan Gong 檀弓 · Than Kung · Tan Gong I.ii.28 … Tan Gong I.ii.38

items.text: When you mourn a parent, proceed through the funeral rites in their set order and do not bring the bier back once the departure sacrifice is done.
items.quote: The proceedings go on in this way to what is more remote, and hence in the details of mourning there is a constant advance and no receding.

items.text: Mourn your father and mother with sincere grief, but do not go beyond the ancient rules or fall short of them.
items.quote: The ancient kings framed the rules of ceremony, and I do not dare not to come up to them.

items.text: Do not sell your half-brothers' mother to pay for your own mother's burial; you cannot sell another man's mother to bury your own.
items.quote: How can we sell the mothers of other men to bury our mother? ... that cannot be done.

items.text: Do not enrich your own family from a parent's funeral gifts; give what is left to the poor among your kindred.
items.quote: a superior man will not enrich his family by means of his mourning. Let us distribute it among the poor of our brethren.

items.text: In a house's mourning, uphold the rightful son and let him take his place as chief mourner.
items.quote: supporting the rightful son to take his position with his face to the south

items.text: Provide sacrificial vessels for your deceased parent's rites, but do not finance them by taking funeral gifts meant for the poor.
items.quote: Dze-shih wished to take what remained of the money and other things contributed towards their expenses, to provide sacrificial vessels
items.conflict: Offerings to the dead are rejected because the dead do not hear; God alone is to be worshiped (Deut 26:14; 1 Tim 2:5).

heading: Liji 2 · Tan Gong 檀弓 · Than Kung · Tan Gong I.i.1 … Tan Gong I.i.12

items.text: Appoint the grandson as successor; do not pass him over for a younger son.
items.quote: Nay, (the rule is to) appoint the grandson.

items.text: Conceal his faults and do not openly or strongly remonstrate with him about them.
items.quote: In serving his father, (a son) should conceal (his faults), and not openly or strongly remonstrate with him about them.

items.text: Wait on and nourish him in every possible way, and serve him laboriously until death.
items.quote: should in every possible way wait on and nourish him, without being tied to definite rules; should serve him laboriously till his death

items.text: Complete the three years' mourning for your father.
items.quote: and then complete the mourning for him for three' years.

items.text: When placing objects in the coffin and grave, be sincere and faithful so that you will have no occasion for regret.
items.quote: a son should exercise sincerity and good faith in regard to everything that is placed with it, so that there shall be no occasion for repentance.

items.text: Do not forget your parents when they are out of sight, and do not listen to music on the anniversary of a parent's death.
items.quote: though (his parents) are out of sight, a son does not forget them ... on the anniversary of a parent's death, he does not listen to music.

items.text: Do not observe mourning for a divorced mother; treat her as no longer your mother.
items.quote: while she was my wife, she was Pâi's mother; but when she ceased to be my wife, she was no longer his mother.
items.conflict: Honor your father and your mother (Exodus 20:12); divorce does not end a mother's motherhood.

heading: Liji 2 · Tan Gong 檀弓 · Than Kung · Tan Gong II.iii.17 … Tan Gong II.iii.25

items.text: If a son kills his father, everyone in his house must put him to death without mercy.
items.quote: When a son kills his father, all who are in the house with him should kill him without mercy.
items.conflict: Private vengeance is forbidden; the civil magistrate, not household members, bears the sword (Rom. 13:4).

items.text: Do not forget your kinship; do not cast off a relation.
items.quote: relations should not forget their relationship, nor old acquaintances their friendship.

heading: Liji 2 · Tan Gong 檀弓 · Than Kung · Tan Gong II.ii.4 … Tan Gong II.ii.11

items.text: At your father's burial, keep offerings modest; where the state is extravagant, show economy.
items.quote: At the burial of his father, he had only one small carriage... he returned immediately from the grave.

items.text: At your mother's interment, act as sole host and place the women behind the men.
items.quote: Let the guests be the guests, while I (alone) act as the host. Let the women take their places behind the men.

items.text: Do not appear before your husband's parents without proper outer garment.
items.quote: A wife does not dare to see her husband's parents without the ornament (of her upper robes)

items.text: Provide the shroud, the funeral offerings, and the food after interment, so the living are not revolted from the dead.
items.quote: Immediately after death, the dried flesh and pickled meats are set out... after the interment, there is the food presented.
items.conflict: Offerings to the dead imply they need them; Scripture forbids this (Deut 18:11; Deut 26:14).

items.text: Let the ritual gestures of mourning—beating the breast and leaping—be practiced as regulated expressions of grief.
items.quote: The observances to regulate all this are what are called the rules of propriety.

items.text: After your father's death, show the prescribed demeanor: first grave and searching, then expectant, then sad as if waiting.
items.quote: Immediately after the death (of his father), he looked grave and restless... After the interment he looked sad.

heading: Liji 2 · Tan Gong 檀弓 · Than Kung · Tan Gong II.iii.6 … Tan Gong II.iii.16

items.text: Offer the repose sacrifice: appoint a personator for the dead and set out a stool with mat and viands for him.
items.quote: At the sacrifice of Repose a personator of the dead is appointed, and a stool, with a mat and viands on it, is placed (for him).
items.conflict: Offerings to the dead; worship God alone (Deut 18:10-12)

items.text: After the wailing is over, avoid uttering the name of the newly deceased.
items.quote: When the wailing is over, the name of the deceased is avoided.

items.text: While mourning your father, do not attend to your own comfort; rather be eager to place his spirit-tablet in the temple.
items.quote: he has to be concerned that (his father's spirit-tablet) is not (yet) in the temple.
items.conflict: Ancestor veneration; worship God alone (Exod 20:3-5)

items.text: Do not emaciate yourself to the endangering of your life while mourning your father, lest you leave him no posterity.
items.quote: nor, in emaciating himself, should he do so to the endangering of his life

items.text: Bury a deceased son in his ordinary clothes and raise only a low mound enough to cover the grave.
items.quote: The grave-clothes were such as (the deceased) had ordinarily worn... he raised a mound over the grave of dimensions sufficient to cover it.

items.text: If your mother died after marrying into another family, do not wail for her in the ancestral temple; mourn for her in a side room.
items.quote: Your mother is dead, after marrying into another family... he wailed in one of the smaller apartments of his house.

items.text: If your father's shrine is burned, wail for it three days.
items.quote: When the (shrine-)apartment of his father was burned, (the ruler) wailed for it three days.
items.conflict: Ancestor veneration; worship God alone (Exod 20:3-5)

heading: Liji 2 · Tan Gong 檀弓 · Than Kung · Tan Gong II.i.29 … Tan Gong II.ii.3

items.text: Bare your shoulders, bind up your hair with the sackcloth band, and remove your usual ornaments to show the changes of grief.
items.quote: Baring the shoulders and binding up the hair (with the band of sackcloth) are changes, (showing) the excited feeling which is a change in the grief.

items.text: On returning from the grave to wail, ascend the hall of the ancestral temple where the departed performed his rites.
items.quote: On returning (from the grave) to wail, (the son) should ascend the hall (of the ancestral temple);--returning to the place where (the deceased) performed his rites.

items.text: On returning from the grave to wail, enter the chamber where the departed received his nourishment.
items.quote: The presiding wife should enter the chamber;--returning to the place where he received his nourishment.

items.text: Present condolences to the son when he returns from the grave and is wailing, for his grief is then at its height.
items.quote: Condolences should be presented (to the son) when he returns (from the grave) and is wailing, at which time his grief is at its height.

items.text: When the coffin has been lowered into the grave, present the ruler's gifts to the dead in the grave.
items.quote: When the coffin has been let down into the grave, the chief mourner presents the (ruler's) gifts (to the dead in the grave)
items.conflict: The dead cannot receive gifts; offerings to the dead are forbidden by God.

items.text: Offer the sacrifice of repose on the day of burial; do not leave the departed a single day without a resting-place.
items.quote: The sacrifice is offered on the day of interment; they cannot bear that the departed should be left a single day (without a place to rest in).
items.conflict: Sacrifices for the dead are not prescribed by God and deny that man dies once and faces judgment.

items.text: Place the spirit-tablet of the departed next to that of his grandfather the day after burial.
items.quote: The next day the service of placing the spirit-tablet of the departed next to that of his grandfather was performed.
items.conflict: Venerating a spirit-tablet is idolatry; the dead are not present in a tablet.

items.text: Bring the coffined dead into the ancestral temple before burial, in accordance with his filial heart.
items.quote: He is (supposed to be) grieved at leaving his chamber, and therefore he is brought to the temple of his fathers
items.conflict: The temple is for God alone; the dead should not be worshiped or venerated there.

items.text: Furnish the grave with spirit vessels of clay and straw, not usable vessels or human-like automata, lest you be led to bury the living with the dead.
items.quote: Confucius said that the making of the straw figures was good, and that the making of the (wooden) automaton was not benevolent.
items.conflict: Providing grave goods for the dead assumes they can use them, but the dead know nothing.

heading: Liji 2 · Tan Gong 檀弓 · Than Kung · Tan Gong II.ii.12 … Tan Gong II.ii.19

items.text: Ask the ruler to fix your father's posthumous title before burying him.
items.quote: The sun and moon have brought the time;--we are about to bury him. I beg that you will fix the title, for which we shall change his name.

items.text: When mourning a parent, do not bathe or put on girdle-pendants with their gems.
items.quote: Whoever, being engaged with the mourning rites for a parent, bathed his head or his body, and put on his girdle-pendants?

items.text: Refuse to bury your father's concubines alive with him; burying the living with the dead is contrary to propriety.
items.quote: To bury the living with the dead is contrary to propriety; how much more must it be so to bury them in the same coffin!

items.text: Nourish your parents while they live, though only with bean soup and water.
items.quote: Bean soup, and water to drink, while the parents are made happy, may be pronounced filial piety.

items.text: When your parents die and you have little means, wrap the body from head to foot and bury it promptly without a shell.
items.quote: wrap the body round from head to foot, and inter it immediately, without a shell, that being all which his means allow

heading: Liji 2 · Tan Gong 檀弓 · Than Kung · Tan Gong II.i.11 … Tan Gong II.i.28

items.text: In mourning for your father, hold loving regard for him precious; do not use his death to seek your own profit.
items.quote: but a loving regard for your father is to be considered precious... if you take advantage of it to seek your own profit

items.text: Observe the mourning rites as the extreme expression of grief and sorrow, remembering those to whom you owe your being.
items.quote: The rites of mourning are the extreme expression of grief and sorrow... mindful of those to whom we owe our being.

items.text: When your wife's brother dies, wail for him in the principal chamber and appoint your son to preside.
items.quote: On the death of his wife's brother... he should wail for him in (the court of) the principal chamber. He should appoint his (own) son to preside.

items.text: If your parent's coffin is in the hall and you hear of a cousin's death, wail for him in a side apartment.
items.quote: If a man have the coffin of a parent in his hall, and hear of mourning going on for a cousin... he wails for him in a side apartment.

items.text: Call the soul of the dead back; look for its return from the dark region among the spirits.
items.quote: Calling (the soul) back... looking for it to return from the dark region is a way of seeking for it among the spiritual beings.
items.conflict: Deuteronomy 18:10-12 forbids seeking the dead.

items.text: Make the inscribed banner and spirit tablet for your deceased father; by it keep his memory and show him reverence.
items.quote: the son by this flag maintains the remembrance of him. From his love for him he makes this record.
items.conflict: Veneration of ancestral tablets and images conflicts with the Second Commandment.

items.text: Offer the sacrifices to the dead with a pure and reverent heart, even though you do not know whether the spirit enjoys them.
items.quote: The offerings to the unburied dead are placed in plain unornamented vessels... He is guided only by his pure and reverent heart.
items.conflict: Offerings to the dead are not commanded; God alone is to be worshiped (Exodus 20:3-5).

items.text: If you are a son by an inferior wife, do not receive condolences at the mourning rites for a great officer.
items.quote: At the mourning rites for a Great officer, a son by an inferior wife should not receive the condolences.
items.conflict: Galatians 3:28; no second-class sons, and concubinage is contrary to Genesis 2:24.

heading: Liji 2 · Tan Gong 檀弓 · Than Kung · Tan Gong I.iii.32 … Tan Gong II.i.10

items.text: After coffining, provide the materials for the shell and the vessels to the eye of fancy.
items.quote: When the coffining has taken place, in ten days after, provision should be made for the materials (for the shell), and for the vessels to the eye of fancy.

items.text: Set forth the morning offering beside the body at sunrise and the evening offering at sunset.
items.quote: The morning offerings should be set forth (beside the body) at sunrise; the evening when the sun is about to set.
items.conflict: Offerings to the dead conflict with the finished work of Christ (Heb. 10:12).

items.text: In mourning for a parent, do not restrict your wailing to set times.
items.quote: In mourning for a parent, there is no restriction to (set) times for wailing.

items.text: When sent on a mission, announce your return to the spirits of your departed parent.
items.quote: If one be sent on a mission, he must announce his return (to the spirits of his departed).
items.conflict: Communicating with the dead is forbidden in Scripture (Deut. 18:11).

items.text: When your parent's corpse is coffined and you hear of a distant cousin's mourning, go and condole with him.
items.quote: if the son hear of mourning going on for a cousin at a distance, he must go (to condole)

items.text: Do not give away anything belonging to the family without the order of your father or elder brother.
items.quote: he ought to have the order of his father or elder brother for the act.

items.text: Complete the twenty-fourth month of mourning, perform the service for leaving off mourning, and wait another month before returning to music.
items.quote: After the service on the conclusion of the twenty-fourth month of mourning... after another month (the mourners) may take to their music.

items.text: Do not go beyond the boundaries of the state on a visit of condolence.
items.quote: A wife should not go beyond the boundaries of the state on a visit of condolence.

heading: Liji 2 · Tan Gong 檀弓 · Than Kung · Tan Gong I.iii.7 … Tan Gong I.iii.31

items.text: Wear the one year's mourning for a brother of the same mother but a different father.
items.quote: the people of Lû wear the one year's mourning in such a case.

items.text: When mourning your mother, do not observe rites beyond your means or at an unsuitable time; act as a superior man would.
items.quote: when there are certain ceremonies to be observed, and he has not the necessary means for them, a superior man does not observe them

items.text: Mourn every kinsman above and below you according to his relationship, and do not reduce the degree of mourning.
items.quote: the ancients made no diminution (in the degrees of mourning on any other ground); but mourned for every one above and below him according to his relationship.

items.text: Think long and carefully about all mourning rites, and see that your parent's coffin is equally well finished inside and out.
items.quote: a son should certainly think deeply and long about them all, and that in buying the coffin he should see that, inside and outside, it be equally well completed

items.text: Place the offerings to the dead at the time of the slighter dressing on the east of the corpse.
items.quote: With regard to the offerings to the dead at the time of the slighter dressing, Dze-yû said that they should be placed on the east (of the corpse).
items.conflict: Offerings to the dead conflict with Scripture: the dead do not receive offerings.

items.text: Arrange for assistance in the house when mourning your mother; to do without is a careless omission.
items.quote: At the mourning rites for the mother of Tû Khiâo no one was employed in the house to assist (the son in the ceremonies), which was accounted a careless omission.

items.text: As soon as a death occurs, change your lambskin furs and dark-colored caps.
items.quote: As soon as a death occurs, (the members of the family) should change their lambskin furs and dark-coloured caps

items.text: Provide funeral articles according to the family's means: if rich, do not exceed the prescribed rites; if poor, simply cover and bury without blame.
items.quote: Where there are means, let there be no exceeding the prescribed rites. If there be a want of means, let the body be lightly covered from head to foot

items.text: Present the new offerings of grain or fruits beside the body in the coffin as abundantly as the offerings on the first of the month.
items.quote: When new offerings (of grain or fruits) are presented (beside the body in the coffin), they should be (abundant), like the offerings on the first day of the moon.
items.conflict: Offerings to the dead conflict with Scripture: the dead do not receive offerings.

items.text: After the burial, each mourner should change his mourning dress.
items.quote: When the interment has taken place, everyone should make a change in his mourning dress.

heading: Liji 2 · Tan Gong 檀弓 · Than Kung · Tan Gong II.iii.26 … Tan Gong II.iii.30

items.text: Observe the mourning proper for a parent-in-law; wear the prescribed garment without adding beyond the rites.
items.quote: Dze-liû's wife... wore for him the one year's mourning... Shû-kung Khien... requested that she should wear the three months' mourning and the simple headband.

items.text: Mourn an elder brother when he dies; do not neglect the mourning.
items.quote: There was a man of Khang, who did not go into mourning on the death of his elder brother.

items.text: When your mother dies, mourn her with fasting and heartfelt grief; do not let custom suppress your sorrow.
items.quote: When Yo Kang, Dze-khun's mother, died, he was five days without eating.

items.text: Direct your wife in the proper mourning for your kin; do not allow her to go beyond the rites.
items.quote: When he withdrew, however, (Dze-liû) made his wife wear the three months' mourning and the simple headband.

heading: Liji 2 · Tan Gong 檀弓 · Than Kung · Tan Gong II.ii.20 … Tan Gong II.iii.5

items.text: Bury your mother in the customary way; do not try out your own mechanical devices on her.
items.quote: could you not in the case of your own mother do so? Would that distress you?

items.text: When leaving your state, wail at the graves of your fathers; on returning, look at the graves before entering the city.
items.quote: when one is leaving his state, he wails at the graves (of his fathers), and then takes his journey
items.conflict: Ancestor veneration may conflict with exclusive worship of God.

items.text: When passing a grave, bow forward to the cross-bar; when passing a place of sacrifice, dismount.
items.quote: when you pass by a grave, you should bow forward to the cross-bar, and, when you pass a place of sacrifice, you should dismount
items.conflict: Bowing to graves may involve undue reverence for the dead.

items.text: Receive condolences for your husband only in the proper place, not on the road.
items.quote: there is the poor cottage of his father. This is not the place where the ruler should demean himself to send me a message

items.text: Do not use rites above your son's rank at his funeral.
items.quote: The three ministers, not employing (such a carriage), and yet employing the sprinklers, thus appropriate a ceremony which is not suitable for them

items.text: Do not wear the mourning of a wife for a concubine, even if she bore you a son.
items.quote: The people of Lû will have it that she, was my wife.
items.conflict: Concubinage and treating a concubine as wife conflict with monogamous marriage.

heading: Liji 2 · Tan Gong 檀弓 · Than Kung · Tan Gong I.i.26 … Tan Gong I.ii.15

items.text: Mourn your sister for the prescribed period; do not prolong mourning beyond the ancient rules.
items.citation: Liji, Tan Gong I.i.26 … Tan Gong I.ii.15
items.quote: When the ancient kings framed their rules, (they might have said that) they could not bear (to cease mourning) even for (ordinary) men on the roads.

items.text: Never forget the ancestor from whom you are descended; in burial and ceremony, keep your root before you.
items.citation: Liji, Tan Gong I.i.26 … Tan Gong I.ii.15
items.quote: In ceremonies, we do not forget him to whom we trace our root.

items.text: Mourn your mother for the prescribed year; do not prolong your wailing beyond the set term.
items.citation: Liji, Tan Gong I.i.26 … Tan Gong I.ii.15
items.quote: Ah! (such a demonstration) is excessive.

items.text: During the nine months' mourning, lay aside your musical studies.
items.citation: Liji, Tan Gong I.i.26 … Tan Gong I.ii.15
items.quote: During the mourning for nine months one should suspend his (musical) studies.

items.text: Set out whatever food remains as offerings by the side of the corpse.
items.citation: Liji, Tan Gong I.i.26 … Tan Gong I.ii.15
items.quote: May not what remains in the cupboard suffice to set down (as the offerings) by (the corpse of) one who has just died?
items.conflict: Offering food to the dead conflicts with the second commandment and the sufficiency of Christ's work.

items.text: For a sister-in-law's five-month mourning, assign a place for wailing; let your wife lead the stamping.
items.citation: Liji, Tan Gong I.i.26 … Tan Gong I.ii.15
items.quote: When Dze-sze wailed for his sister-in-law, he made such places, and his wife took the lead in the stamping.

items.text: In mourning for a parent, abstain from food and drink for three days only; use your staff to rise.
items.citation: Liji, Tan Gong I.i.26 … Tan Gong I.ii.15
items.quote: no water or other liquid enters his mouth for three days, and with the aid of his staff he is still able to rise.

items.text: Even if news of a brother's death arrives late, still put on mourning for him.
items.citation: Liji, Tan Gong I.i.26 … Tan Gong I.ii.15
items.quote: when brethren are far apart there would be no wearing of mourning for them at all; and would this be right?

items.text: Wail for a brother in the ancestral temple.
items.citation: Liji, Tan Gong I.i.26 … Tan Gong I.ii.15
items.quote: For brethren, I wail in the ancestral temple.

items.text: Do not let mourning for a son destroy your health; moderate your grief.
items.citation: Liji, Tan Gong I.i.26 … Tan Gong I.ii.15
items.quote: When you mourned for your son, you did it in such a way that you have lost your eyesight.

items.text: Do not pass the night away from your inner chamber without great cause; do not stay closeted inside all day and night unless fasting or ill.
items.citation: Liji, Tan Gong I.i.26 … Tan Gong I.ii.15
items.quote: does not pass the night outside (his chamber); and unless he is carrying out a fast or is ill, he does not day and night stop inside.

items.text: When mourning a mother, wear sackcloth with even edges; sit upright and do no heavy labor.
items.citation: Liji, Tan Gong I.i.26 … Tan Gong I.ii.15
items.quote: When wearing the sackcloth with the edges even (for a mother), one should not sit unevenly or to one side, nor should he do any toilsome labour
